reference_sql:
SELECT s.store_code, o.order_id
FROM stores s
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-04 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-05 00:00:00'
alternatives: SELECT s.store_code, o.order_id FROM orders o RIGHT JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-04 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-05 00:00:00'
SELECT s.store_code, o.order_id FROM stores s LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id AND CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) = DATE '2025-03-04'

other_way.sql: SELECT s.store_code, o.order_id FROM orders o RIGHT JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-04 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-05 00:00:00'
other_way.tradeoff: Writing orders first and stores after RIGHT JOIN lists the same rows, but the question starts from the stores, as the LEFT JOIN does.
